alternativeText.text: An electric circuit with a red wire, a battery, a lightbulb and a black wire. The red wire connects one end of the battery to the  light bulb. The black wire connects the light bulb to the other end of the battery. The battery is labeled voltage source, the lightbulb is labeled resistive component, and the wires are labeled conducting path.

textContent.text: Electric circuits are used to power many different appliances. Every circuit contains at least three components: a voltage source, a conducting path, and a resistive component.
The model shown here represents a circuit used to power a flashlight. This circuit contains only a few components, but other circuits can be more complex.

pieces.text: can be created. These diagrams use symbols to represent each circuit component.

table.text: A battery is a type of voltage source and is represented with two line segments of different lengths. The longer vertical line represents the positive terminal, and the shorter vertical line represents the negative terminal. Electric current flows away from the positive terminal and toward the negative terminal.
A resistor is represented with a zigzag. This symbol is used to represent any resistive component, such as a light bulb or heating element.
A wire is represented with a straight line. Wires serve as a conducting path to connect the other components and form a closed circuit.
